fields: [pic=4]As you can guess, I take on the roll of the Bell Bearer.
[pic=3]Partly to play out the role, but also…
[pic=5]I do go on look out for any critters that might be struggling in the cold.
[pic=3]There has been a few occasions where I have found critters in need of help. Much like how I found you!
[pic=4]But mainly I just go around visiting other areas. It’s always nice seeing other critters ringing out their bells to me in celebration too!
[pic=3]But my experience of the celebration is a bit different than the other critters here…
[pic=11]He insists that there is this "Saint" character that played a role during the Blessing.
[pic=8]But that’s not how I’ve heard it.
[pic=2]In any case, there’s a whole other part of the festivities that I don’t partake in because I’m prepping for the actual Blessing.
I see! Ok, I will talk to him.
[pic=2]Thanks for asking about this though! I’m happy to teach folks about this since it’s a time that’s very close to my heart!
[pic=5]Critters had no choice but to band together. They would exchange and share provisions, huddle for warmth, and share in eachother’s company.
[pic=8]But they knew it wouldn’t last, they knew they needed help.
[pic=5]So each night, when the weather was the most still, the critters would ring their bells for hope that anyone would hear it.
[pic=5]Day after day, new critters would show up, share in the warmth and comfort others could provide, and night after night, they would ring their bells.
[pic=5]Weeks went by. Until finally, on the 18th night, a heavy sound rung out from the skies.
[pic=4]The familiar sound of a bell, but this one was much larger… It grew louder and louder. It was coming closer!
[pic=10]On the 19th night, a great falcon was spotted in the distance.
[pic=10]The bird carried a tremendous bell, ringing out far into the night.
[pic=1]The critters calls were heard, they were answered!
[pic=7]The Falcon circled overhead, ringing out their giant bell. And the critters joined in with their own chorus of bells!
[pic=4]Within hours, a rescue team came barreling after the falcon, providing food and water to all.
[pic=3]Thus, The Blessing of the Bells became a widespread story. A necessity for winter survival back in the day.
[pic=1]I go flying around with a BIG OLE BELL ringing across the lands!
[pic=4]Critters down below will join me ringing out their own bells as I pass by. It’s a wonderful time!
[pic=1]It really is! It’s a magical time, and I’m super grateful I can be a part of it!
[pic=3]Did Scarlett tell you why this is a holiday at all? Where it all started?
She said I should hear it from you.
[pic=3]Well The Blessing of the Bells has become much more superficial these days.
[pic=3]Gift giving, partying, decorations, friends and family, y’know how it goes…
[pic=8]But it actually started in much darker times…
[pic=5]Long ago, the Winters were very harsh, and times were much tougher. Provisions were harder to come by, and larger communities like ours were quite scarce.
[pic=8]Snowy seasons were quite dangerous. If a family didn’t prepare, there were dire consequences…
[pic=8]One terrible Winter, the winds blew harder than ever, the snow was relentless, the temperatures were unbearable.
[pic=1]Oh it’s a wonderful time! Lots of the critters here get into the spirit of things.
[pic=2]I hope you’ll join us for the next one!

I’d like to!
Can you tell me more about it?
[pic=2]It’s a month long celebration, where critters bundle up, decorate their surroundings, share gifts and meals!
[pic=4]We close out each night of celebration with a ringing of a bell!
[pic=1]Then do the whole thing over the next day!
[pic=4]It is! And that’s not even the best part!
[pic=6]The very last day, yours truly finishes the entire celebration with "The Blessing!"

I’ve heard you know a thing or two
about The Blessing of the Bells?
